subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Burning and annoying sensation at the tick bite site.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 68 years old and male. I came in because I got a tick bite around my knee a week ago, and it's been burning and annoying me. I'm not sure if it's anything serious, but I thought I should check it out. Doctor: Can you describe the appearance of the tick bite, including its size, color, and whether there is any surrounding redness or swelling? Have you noticed any other symptoms such as fever, chills, headache, or a rash since the tick bite? Was the tick removed, and if so, how? Patient: The tick bite is around my knee, and it's been there for over a week. It just burns and is kind of annoying. It feels warm on that spot, but I haven't had any fever or chills. I didn't really notice any other symptoms except for a little headache and not feeling quite well in general since the bite. I didn't remove the tick myself; I just noticed the bite. Doctor: Have you noticed any rash, swelling, or changes in the appearance of the tick bite site since the incident? Patient: Yes, I have noticed a rash around the bite area. It's kind of a bull's-eye looking rash, and there's some redness and swelling. It doesn't hurt too bad, but it does feel warm and a little sore when I press on it. Doctor: Have you traveled to any areas known for high tick activity in the past month, and have you been exposed to any other potential sources of infection? Patient: I've been out in the woods and spending a lot of time in my yard, which is probably where I got the tick bite. I also went hunting a couple of weeks ago, so I guess that's another place I could have been exposed to ticks. I haven't traveled anywhere else recently. Doctor: Have you experienced any neurological symptoms such as tingling, numbness

Doctor: Have you traveled to any areas known for high tick activity in the past month, and have you been exposed to any other potential sources of infection? Patient: I've been out in the woods and spending a lot of time in my yard, which is probably where I got the tick bite. I also went hunting a couple of weeks ago, so I guess that's another place I could have been exposed to ticks. I haven't traveled anywhere else recently. Doctor: Have you experienced any neurological symptoms such as tingling, numbness
